one_line: Agent-assisted realtime dashboard builder for marketing analytics.
what_it_does: Creates and edits dashboards through WebMCP while showing the visual effects in realtime, with widgets, filters, and data-source-driven charts.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP is central: the agent can inspect datasource fields and construct dashboard widgets while the human observes shared live state. General UI driving could reproduce it, but with materially more friction and less precision.
leverage_evidence: Pitch explicitly says dashboards are created through WebMCP with realtime effects.
Frame sheets show a populated analytics dashboard plus editor/inspector controls and multiple chart types.
About text describes describeDatasource and addWidget tool-driven editing.
execution_rationale: The packet shows coherent dashboard and editor surfaces with populated KPIs, charts, tables, and configuration panels, but no transcript or live end-to-end proof and the frame sheets are low-resolution.
execution_evidence: Frames show KPI cards, bar/line/pie/gauge visualizations, tables, and an editor inspector.
Devpost screenshot shows a concrete dashboard demo preview with configurable dimensions, metrics, filters, and breakdowns.
impact_rationale: Marketing and advertising teams have a clear recurring need for client-facing performance dashboards; reducing manual dashboard construction and preserving creator intent is credible value.
impact_evidence: About text identifies product engineers, agencies, and clients as the audience and describes recurring campaign reporting work.
Visible dashboard includes marketing metrics and campaign breakdowns.
creativity_rationale: The concept is a fresh combination of natural-language agent construction and visual dashboard editing, though dashboard builders themselves are an established category.
creativity_evidence: The submission frames WebMCP as a shared text-to-visual dashboard authoring interaction.
Frames show generated report presentation alongside a conventional fine-tuning editor.
usability_note: The visual editor, inspector, and realtime output suggest a usable workflow; small text and some sparse states limit certainty.
red_flags: No submitted video/transcript despite frame sheets.
Some frame states appear sparse or placeholder-like.
standouts: Strong shared-state agent/editor concept.
Concrete marketing dashboard vocabulary and varied visualization support.
advance_reason: Strong WebMCP leverage and credible product value, with enough visual evidence of a coherent dashboard workflow to advance.

one_line: Agent prepares, pays for, and tracks physical letters and postcards.
what_it_does: Connects an agent to PieterPost so it can write or upload content, prepare mail, create payment, check status, and cancel orders with human control.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP turns a multi-step physical fulfillment workflow into a structured conversation spanning preparation, payment, and tracking. A general UI agent would face substantial form, upload, payment, and later-status friction.
leverage_evidence: About text lists seven structured tools covering upload, preparation, payment links, order status, cancellation, and orders.
Devpost media visibly depicts an AI-generated letter, confirmation gate, payment flow, and PieterPost preparation state.
Human confirmation is retained before transmitting data and payment.
execution_rationale: The packet presents a coherent product and a plausible complete workflow, but still imagery and no transcript cannot verify that a physical item was actually mailed.
execution_evidence: Frame sheets show payment/Apple Pay and cross-device continuation states.
Devpost screenshot shows the letter-preparation flow and confirmation-oriented UI.
impact_rationale: Sending physical notices, invoices, cancellation requests, and personal mail is a real task with meaningful convenience value for consumers and organizations.
impact_evidence: Pitch names invoices, cancellation requests, documents, letters, and birthday cards.
The product connects digital composition to physical postal fulfillment.
creativity_rationale: The memorable concept is an agent completing a real-world postal workflow rather than stopping at text generation; payment and tracking deepen the interaction.
creativity_evidence: Physical mail fulfillment is unusually concrete for an agent workflow.
Submission tagline and screenshots show the full prompt-to-post framing.
usability_note: Structured results, safe retries, cancellation, and human payment control suggest good usability; actual live access is not independently observed.
red_flags: No transcript and static frames cannot prove final mailing.
Payment and personal-address handling require trust and privacy scrutiny.
standouts: End-to-end bridge from agent text to physical-world fulfillment.
Human approval gates are clearly integrated.
advance_reason: High WebMCP delta, specific audience value, and unusually concrete real-world outcome.

one_line: Shared human-agent planner for astronomical observing nights.
what_it_does: Computes darkness, Moon, target visibility, and observing plans locally, then lets an agent rank nights, point a live sky map, revise ghost plans around human favorites, revalidate sites, and export.
leverage_rationale: The agent and human operate the same live sky instrument: the agent reads gestures and state, proposes uncommitted plans, points the map, and revalidates portable plans. This structured shared state is central and difficult to replicate comparably through generic UI driving.
leverage_evidence: Transcript explicitly describes fifteen tools, eleven always live, shared map state, gesture-readable favorites, ghost plans, confirmation, and site revalidation.
Frames visibly show the sky map moving among targets, favorites, and ranked-night captions.
About text says all astronomy runs locally and the agent uses the same instrument as the human.
execution_rationale: This is the strongest evidenced packet: the 168-second video transcript describes a complete workflow and frame sheets show corresponding map, target, favorite, and planning states.
execution_evidence: Transcript covers prompt, ranked date, target selection, favorites, ghost plan confirmation, site switch, revalidation, and export.
Frames show star map, target labels including Andromeda, Saturn, and Pleiades, and gesture instructions.
Devpost screenshot clearly identifies the product and demo.
impact_rationale: Amateur astronomers, educators, and observatory operators have a real planning problem; the tool credibly reduces tedious calculations while preserving human review.
impact_evidence: Transcript identifies night-sky planning difficulty and a three-hour observing use case.
About text describes target windows, darkness, Moon conditions, and portability across sites.
creativity_rationale: The one-instrument-two-operators interaction, gesture-to-agent preference transfer, ghost plans, and portable site revalidation form a highly original and memorable concept.
creativity_evidence: Human taps the sky and agent incorporates favorites without typing.
Plan is explicitly marked as site-specific and revalidated when moved to Mauna Kea.
Cinematic demo pursues the concept deeply rather than showing a superficial wrapper.
usability_note: The staged ghost-plan confirmation and visible map movement support a clear human-in-the-loop workflow.
standouts: Exceptional shared live state between agent and human.
Complete, domain-authentic workflow with excellent video evidence.
advance_reason: Top-tier leverage, execution evidence, and creativity; the packet demonstrates WebMCP as the interaction model rather than an add-on.

one_line: Cited agent-callable college transfer and Canvas counselor.
what_it_does: Uses structured tools over official transfer agreements and read-only Canvas data to audit courses, compare campuses, explain requirements, surface risk and deadlines, and set reminders.
leverage_rationale: Structured tools let the agent query deterministic academic records and cited outputs while exposing activity to the student. General UI automation would be less reliable across complex transfer data and Canvas state.
leverage_evidence: Pitch and about text describe thirteen WebMCP tools over ASSIST, catalog, and Canvas.
Devpost screenshot visibly shows target campus, major, coursework, grades, and upcoming work in one interface.
The design makes every call visible in an activity feed and returns citations.
execution_rationale: The visual packet shows a coherent counselor interface, but no video, transcript, gallery image, or end-to-end tool invocation proof; execution is capped by thin evidence.
execution_evidence: Devpost thumbnail shows transfer target, major, course list, coursework, and deadlines.
About text specifies deterministic engine and read-only Canvas proxy, but these are claims not directly observed.
impact_rationale: Transfer students, especially first-generation and working students, face a consequential fragmented-information problem; cited personalized guidance could materially improve decisions.
impact_evidence: About text identifies community-college transfer barriers and first-generation/working students.
The demonstrated UI combines transfer agreements, coursework, grades, and deadlines.
creativity_rationale: The synthesis of transfer articulation, personal Canvas state, citations, and agent access is fresh and thoughtfully scoped, though counseling and degree-audit tools are known categories.
creativity_evidence: The project claims to answer cross-campus comparisons that ASSIST does not directly provide.
Structured-in/cited-out deterministic counseling is a meaningful interaction choice.
usability_note: The consolidated dashboard and visible activity feed appear student-friendly; Canvas login and unverified live behavior remain unknown.
red_flags: No submitted video or frame evidence beyond a static Devpost thumbnail.
High-stakes academic data accuracy and authentication need validation.
standouts: Specific underserved audience and strong problem-solution fit.
Citations and deterministic engine are appropriate trust mechanisms.
advance_reason: Excellent impact and strong claimed leverage, though execution confidence is reduced by absent end-to-end evidence.

one_line: Agent-operated workspace that turns rough ideas into product drafts and design previews.
what_it_does: Creates a structured product workspace with BRD, PRD, ERD, flows, screen map, design brief, and interactive prototype through page-scoped WebMCP tools.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP exposes context-aware project inspection, generation, refinement, and design tools directly in the workspace, enabling an agent to operate a multi-artifact product workflow with shared state.
leverage_evidence: Frames visibly show an available-site-tools menu with inspect, generate, refine, and design tool names.
Frames show an explicit generate_product_draft invocation and progress card listing connected artifacts.
About text says tools are page-scoped and reuse existing workflows.
execution_rationale: The packet shows consistent workspace navigation, tool invocation, progress, draft files, confirmed-versus-proposed requirements, and handoff/download controls; the evidence is still mostly montage imagery.
execution_evidence: Frames show generation accepted, composing status, BRD/PRD/ERD/user flows/screen map/design brief outputs, and draft controls.
Devpost screenshot shows a coherent product-builder presentation and demo media.
impact_rationale: Teams and coding agents routinely need clarified product context; turning an idea into structured decisions and a prototype can prevent costly implementation misunderstandings.
impact_evidence: About text explicitly frames the gap between coding agents and product context.
Visible workflow organizes requirements, data model, flows, screens, and design into a handoff.
creativity_rationale: The connected artifact graph and agent-operated product-shaping workflow are a strong, ambitious synthesis beyond simple text generation.
creativity_evidence: One product context feeds six connected artifacts and a multi-screen prototype.
The UI distinguishes confirmed requirements from assumptions/proposals and supports iterative refinement.
usability_note: The staged generation and review controls are promising, though long-running generation and dense artifacts may create friction.
red_flags: Contact sheets are repetitive and small; detailed output quality is hard to inspect.
Some generation states are in-progress rather than fully demonstrated.
standouts: Strong agent-native product-context workflow.
Clear separation of confirmed facts and proposals.
advance_reason: Central WebMCP role and coherent multi-artifact workflow make this a strong advance despite limited video fidelity.

one_line: Human-approved WebMCP ICU shift and risk-review copilot using synthetic data.
what_it_does: Reads changing simulated vitals, ranks patient risk, explains trends, proposes flags/notes/alerts/triage actions, and drafts handoffs while nurses approve changes.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP gives the agent structured access to live risk state and a guarded proposal workflow with provenance and audit records. The nurse sees and commits changes, making shared state meaningful rather than a chatbot overlay.
leverage_evidence: About text specifies read-risk, explain-trend, propose-action, and handoff tools.
Write tools create pending proposals requiring nurse approval; handoff is explicitly co-authored.
Frames show patients-by-risk and approvals-oriented clinical UI.
execution_rationale: The UI and claimed workflow are coherent and visibly staged, but there is no video transcript or live end-to-end evidence and the contact sheets are low-resolution.
execution_evidence: Frames consistently show clinical signal dashboard, patient/risk rows, approvals, and human-decision framing.
Devpost thumbnail visibly shows clinical panels and approval interface.
impact_rationale: ICU handoff and triage coordination are high-stakes problems where provenance, prioritization, and accountable human approval could provide substantial value, even as a simulation.
impact_evidence: About text identifies live-vital changes, handoff coordination, and clear ownership as the problem.
The product explicitly uses synthetic demo data and disclaims clinical use, appropriately limiting the claim.
creativity_rationale: The restrained human-in-the-loop clinical agent model, pending proposals, provenance, and audit trail are a thoughtful and memorable response to the domain.
creativity_evidence: Tagline and UI center human decision rather than autonomous clinical action.
Proposal approval/rejection and co-authored handoff are deliberate interaction choices.
usability_note: Approval gates and audit trail support trust; dense clinical data and high-stakes context require careful interaction design.
red_flags: Synthetic data only; not evidence of clinical validity.
No video/transcript and small frames limit end-to-end verification.
standouts: Strong safety framing and visible human accountability.
WebMCP proposal semantics fit the workflow well.
advance_reason: High-impact, domain-specific human-in-loop workflow with meaningful WebMCP leverage; advance with simulation caveat.

what_it_does: Lets agents search events, compare ticket options, reserve inventory, inspect a shared cart, and prepare checkout while a human retains payment confirmation.
leverage_rationale: Structured search, ticket option, reservation, cart, and checkout-preparation tools improve reliability for a multi-step purchase and synchronize with the human-visible cart, but a general agent could perform much of the same UI flow with friction.
leverage_evidence: About text lists seven tools spanning search through prepare_checkout.
Devpost screenshot shows event search, Noche de Folklore Andino, ticket options, shared cart, and WebMCP panel.
Frames show event/ticket UI and agent activity, but carts remain visibly empty in the captured states.
execution_rationale: The event page and ticket controls are consistently rendered, but the packet does not visibly prove successful reservation, populated cart, checkout preparation, or payment.
execution_evidence: Frames show event details, ticket selection controls, agent activity, and an empty-cart state.
Devpost screenshot presents the claimed workflow but is a static video thumbnail.
impact_rationale: Ticket discovery and reservation are real consumer needs, and focusing on Bolivian cultural events gives the product a specific community audience with credible cultural value.
impact_evidence: Pitch targets Bolivian cultural events and shared human-agent purchase decisions.
Visible event listing and ticket-selection experience support the use case.
creativity_rationale: Agent-native ticketing with shared cart and human checkout is a fresh synthesis, though ticket commerce is an established category.
creativity_evidence: The project emphasizes shared cart state and stopping before payment for explicit human confirmation.
It combines natural-language discovery with standard seat/checkout affordances.
usability_note: The normal event UI is understandable, but the repeated empty-cart/debug-panel states suggest the demonstrated agent flow may be incomplete.
red_flags: Captured carts are empty and no completed reservation or checkout is visible.
Developer-tools panels dominate the visual evidence.
standouts: Specific cultural-event audience.
Human-visible shared cart and payment boundary are sensible.

one_line: WebMCP tool that teleports a coding-agent side task into an isolated sandbox.
what_it_does: Captures context, spawns a separate Daytona browser/terminal session for an independent agent, streams its work, and returns summary, evidence, files, commands, tests, and optional patch.
leverage_rationale: The product uses WebMCP to make agent delegation an in-page action with shared context and a separate execution surface; this is a capability change beyond ordinary UI automation.
leverage_evidence: About text describes teleport_agent, context capture, isolated Daytona sandbox, independent investigation, and returned evidence/patch.
Seven page tools and Socket.io rooms are claimed for separate sessions.
execution_rationale: The packet has a coherent concept and Devpost packaging, but no frame sheets were submitted and the sole screenshot shows blocked media, so actual execution is not evidenced.
execution_evidence: Devpost page identifies the project and describes the teleportation concept.
Embedded media is visibly blocked with a connection-security error.
impact_rationale: Parallelizing debugging while preserving the primary coding task addresses a real productivity bottleneck for agent-assisted development.
impact_evidence: About text gives a concrete stalled-checkout/payment-API debugging scenario.
Returned root cause, commands, tests, and patch are useful outputs for developers.
creativity_rationale: Teleporting a copy of an agent into an isolated computer while the primary agent continues is a distinctive, memorable interaction model with ambitious infrastructure scope.
creativity_evidence: The separate sandbox/room/whiteboard model is more than a simple background job.
The concept explicitly returns an evidence-backed handoff for primary-agent review.
usability_note: The proposed handoff is clear, but no usable flow is visible because the demo media is blocked.
red_flags: No frame sheets submitted.
Devpost embedded media is blocked by a security verification error.
Execution claims cannot be independently checked from this packet.
standouts: Highly original agent-parallelism concept.
Evidence-oriented handoff design is well chosen.
advance_reason: Conceptual leverage and creativity are high, but execution and eligibility remain unclear because the only demo evidence is blocked.

one_line: Human-approved life-event paperwork hub with cross-portal reconciliation.
what_it_does: Turns one life-event sentence into canonical facts, portal-specific drafts, deadline math, conflict reconciliation, approval dialogs, and receipts across agencies, insurers, and employers.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP's page-scoped tools and structured two-call write gates can coordinate several portal workflows while preserving canonical shared state and human approval. Generic UI driving would be substantially more brittle.
leverage_evidence: About text describes dynamically registered per-portal tools, canonical profile, reconciliation, deadlines, and two-call human approval gates.
Frames show prompt-to-result cards and a detailed SSA form with validation/confirmation states.
Devpost screenshot shows prefilled application draft with validate and file controls.
execution_rationale: The packet shows a coherent prompt-to-form workflow and apparent validation/confirmation states, but no transcript or live end-to-end proof of filing across all portals.
execution_evidence: Frames show initial one-sentence prompt, result cards, SSA form, modal confirmation, and green status states.
Devpost media visibly shows canonical-profile prefill, validation, and filing controls.
impact_rationale: Life events generate repetitive, deadline-sensitive paperwork across disconnected portals; reducing re-entry and catching conflicts has direct high value for affected families.
impact_evidence: About text gives a concrete birth/dependent scenario and insurer deadline math.
The UI demonstrates populated fields, validation, and a human-controlled filing sequence.
creativity_rationale: The canonical-facts/reconciliation model, page-scoped portal surfaces, and human-sovereign multi-portal bundle are an ambitious and original interaction model.
creativity_evidence: The product catches name/date normalization conflicts and only standardizes with human consent.
It unifies agency, insurer, and employer paperwork without allowing silent filing.
usability_note: One-sentence intake, visible conflicts, deadline cues, and approval dialogs are strong usability choices; sensitive data handling needs scrutiny.
red_flags: Screenshots include identifiable-looking personal data, though likely demonstration data; privacy handling is not evidenced.
No transcript or proof of actual multi-portal submission receipts.
standouts: Excellent problem specificity and impact.
Strong safety boundary: nothing files without a human click.
advance_reason: Very strong impact, creativity, and WebMCP leverage with visible workflow evidence; advance despite unverified live filing.

execution_evidence: Devpost page has a demo media thumbnail and describes print/photo editing.

creativity_evidence: The concept lets an agent operate visual templates and refer to selected images conversationally.
